title: Your Thesis Title
text:
About this template
The template provides the parts of a thesis that are the same for everyone: a book structure with front matter, an HTML website, three PDF variants, an ePub edition, bibliography and cross-reference handling, executable code cells, and a continuous-integration setup that publishes the website to GitHub Pages. It is derived from redeboer/phd-thesis, with the thesis-specific prose, figures, branding, and scientific dependencies removed.

title: Your Thesis Title
text:
What the example chapters show
The chapters in the sidebar are a tour of the authoring features, not a narrative:

1  Introduction and 5  Conclusion sketch the expected structure of those chapters.
2  Background contains a labelled equation, Equation (2.1), demonstrating numbered equation cross-references in both HTML and LaTeX.
3  Methods embeds an executable Python cell whose figure and numbers are generated during the build and cached between runs. It also demonstrates folded code, hidden input, and format-dependent output.
4  Results shows a cross-referenced table, Table 4.1.
The References page collects citations such as [1; 2], rendered from docs/references.bib through a CSL style. The second entry has 26 authors, so it shows how the IEEE style truncates long author lists with “et al.”.

The same sources produce the downloadable PDF and ePub editions, including paperback and hardcover PDFs with mirrored margins, and an optional Ruhr University Bochum theme.

title: Your Thesis Title
text:
Starting your own thesis

Click Use this template on the repository page and clone the result.
Install Pixi and uv, then run pixi run bootstrap. The guided configuration asks for your title, author details, institution, and repository, writes them into the Quarto configuration, and removes the template-only tooling.
Replace the example chapters and front matter under docs/, add your sources to docs/references.bib, and run pixi run doclive to preview while you write.

The README covers installation, the available build tasks, and publishing in more detail. After bootstrapping, this page becomes the preface of your own thesis.

title: 2  Background
text:
2.1 A sample equation
Review the concepts and literature needed to understand the original work. Prefer synthesis over a catalogue of papers, and make the relationship to the research questions explicit.
Equations can be labelled and referenced using Quarto syntax:
\[
E = mc^2
\tag{2.1}\]
The relation in Equation (2.1) illustrates a numbered cross-reference.

title: 3  Methods
text:
3.1 Reproducible computations
Describe the research design, data, apparatus, software, and analysis choices in enough detail for the work to be assessed and reproduced.
Executable Python, Julia, or R cells can be placed directly in .qmd files. Add the corresponding runtime dependencies to pyproject.toml, use a fixed seed for stochastic calculations, and expose the relevant inputs alongside the results.
The following example creates a small synthetic dataset and fits a straight line. Quarto executes the cell while rendering the thesis and caches its output.
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=2026)
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 25)
y = 1.8 * x + 2.5 + rng.normal(scale=1.5, size=x.size)
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(x, y, deg=1)
The fitted value can also be inserted into the prose as generated Markdown instead of being copied manually:
The fitted slope is 1.81.
Show the plotting code
figure, axis = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.0))
axis.scatter(x, y, label="Synthetic observations")
axis.plot(x, slope * x + intercept, label="Linear fit")
axis.set(xlabel="Independent variable", ylabel="Measured response")
axis.legend()
figure.tight_layout()
plt.show()








Figure 3.1: Synthetic observations and the fitted straight-line model. The fixed random seed makes the figure reproducible.
The generated output can be cited like any static asset; for example, Figure 3.1 shows the result of the calculation above. In a real thesis, the same pattern can generate analysis tables and publication figures directly from the source data.
This page deliberately demonstrates several presentation modes. The setup cell shows its input but suppresses output, the generated sentence hides its input with echo: false, the plotting cell is folded in HTML with a custom summary, the page-level code tools allow readers to reveal or inspect source, and the PDF build hides all cell input while retaining results.
